Port.title: Port
Port.description: Represents a maritime port or terminal where vessels can depart from or arrive at. Admin staff can manage these entries.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Port entity.

name.description: The official or common name of the port.

code.description: A unique short code or identifier for the port, if applicable (e.g., an internal operational code).

city.description: The city where the port is geographically located.

country.description: The country where the port is geographically located.

latitude.description: The geographic latitude coordinate of the port, useful for mapping and location services.

longitude.description: The geographic longitude coordinate of the port, useful for mapping and location services.

description.description: A brief description or additional information about the port facilities or location.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the port record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the port record was last updated.

definition.description: A top-level collection containing all maritime port definitions. Access (create, read, update, delete) is restricted exclusively to admin staff. Authorization is managed via a global admin roles collection (e.g., /roles_admin/{userId}), meaning no denormalized authorization fields are included within the 'Port' document itself.

params.name: portId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific Port entity.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure for managing 'Port' entities leverages a top-level collection to ensure clear security boundaries and adhere to core design principles. All 'Port' documents will reside in the `/ports` collection. This design ensures that all documents within the `/ports` collection share a homogeneous security posture, meaning every port entry requires the same level of authorization for access.

**Authorization Independence:** To achieve authorization independence for 'Port' management, access control will rely on a global role system rather than hierarchical document checks. Admin staff authorization will be determined by checking for the existence of a document in a dedicated global roles collection, typically `/roles_admin/{userId}`. The presence of a document at `/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid)` indicates that the requesting user is an administrator. This approach completely eliminates the need for `get()` operations within security rules for the `/ports` collection, as authorization is resolved externally and atomically. Consequently, 'Port' documents do not require any denormalized authorization fields (like `ownerId` or `members` map) within their own structure, simplifying the schema and reducing data redundancy at the document level.

**QAPs (Query Access Patterns):** By segregating all 'Port' entities into the `/ports` collection and applying an admin-only access rule based on the global `/roles_admin` collection, 'list' operations are inherently secure and efficient. Since all documents in `/ports` have the same security requirements, security rules can grant or deny access to the entire collection based on the user's admin status. This means a client application can perform `list` queries without needing to implement client-side filtering or relying on server-side filters (as rules are not filters), directly supporting the QAP principle. If an admin user queries `/ports`, they will receive all documents; if a non-admin user queries, access will be denied by the rules, ensuring data integrity and performance.
